places: near Kulul within the Danakil Depression

fields.climate: hot, dry desert strip along Red Sea coast; cooler and wetter in the central highlands (up to 61 cm of rainfall annually, heaviest June to September); semiarid in western hills and lowlands
fields.terrain: dominated by extension of Ethiopian north-south trending highlands, descending on the east to a coastal desert plain, on the northwest to hilly terrain and on the southwest to flat-to-rolling plains
fields.hazards: frequent droughts, rare earthquakes and volcanoes; locust swarms; volcanism: Dubbi (1,625 m), which last erupted in 1861, was the country's only historically active volcano until Nabro (2,218 m) came to life in 2011
fields.resources: gold, potash, zinc, copper, salt, possibly oil and natural gas, fish
fields.farm: sorghum, milk, barley, vegetables, root vegetables, cereals, pulses, wheat, beef, maize
fields.exports: copper ore, zinc ore, gold, garments, liquor
fields.industries: food processing, beverages, clothing and textiles, light manufacturing, salt, cement
fields.languages: Tigrinya (official), Arabic (official), English (official), Tigre, Kunama, Afar, other Cushitic languages
fields.religions: Eritrean Orthodox, Roman Catholic, Evangelical Lutheran, Sunni Muslim
fields.legal: mixed system of civil, customary, and Islamic religious law
fields.military: Eritrea mandates military service for all citizens age 18-40; 18-month conscript service obligation, which reportedly includes 4-6 months of military training and 12 months of military or other…
